---
title: The Graph Widget
type: concept
---

Two views of the same data, both reading the same `graph.json`:

- **Full graph view**: place the `{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}` shortcode
  on any page you choose (this project puts it on [[Graph]]) to show every
  page as a node and every resolved wikilink as an edge. Drag nodes,
  scroll to zoom, click a node to open that page. Nothing is
  auto-generated: if you don't add the shortcode anywhere, there's no
  full-graph page at all.
- **Sidebar mini-panel**: on every page, a small 1-hop subgraph (the
  current page plus everything it directly links to or from) mounts at the
  top of the right-hand TOC sidebar. Clicking it opens a larger modal
  version of the same 1-hop view.

Both are drawn by the same client-side canvas widget
(`_extensions/quarto-graph/graph.js`). There's no server, no pre-rendered
image. The browser fetches `graph.json` once per page load and runs a
small force-directed layout (repulsion between all nodes, springs along
edges, gentle centering gravity) until it settles, then stops the
animation loop entirely until you interact with it again.

## Node color

Comes from each page's `type:` frontmatter (see [[Getting Started]]):
`concept` (teal), `person` (purple), `reference` (orange), `project` (deep
red), `experiment` (gold), `moc` (slate blue). Anything else, or no `type:`
at all, falls back to gray.

## If the widget doesn't show up

It's built as progressive enhancement. If `graph.json` 404s, or the fetch
fails for any reason, the widget just does nothing, silently. No error in
the page itself. Check the browser console and the network tab for
`graph.json` first; see [[Under the Hood]] for how it's assembled, and
where that could go missing.
